title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Theater on 1969-04-26
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with very good sound captures a high‑energy early‑'69 show highlighted by Viola Lee, Caution Jam and a wild backing‑tape experiment.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑cleaned SBD source sounds clear and well‑balanced, letting the band’s psychedelic peak shine.  Highlights include the soaring Viola Lee/​Caution jam, a blazing Mountains of the Moon → China Cat → Doin’ That Rag sequence and the infamous backing‑tape “What’s Become of the Baby” interlude; the set is generally high‑energy though a few spots (Hard to Handle, a sluggish It’s a Sin) feel sloppy.  Overall the performance is praised as a rare early‑'69 gem.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ~4.4, strong praise for musical moments and clear soundboard source; only minor technical or performance flaws noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Cleaned and correctly pitched by Miller; generally crisp and balanced with no major drop‑outs, though some reviewers note occasional cymbal muddiness.

standout_songs: Viola Lee > Caution Jam > Viola Lee
Mountains of the Moon → (D) Star Jam → China Cat Sunflower → Doin' That Rag
What's Become of the Baby (backing‑tape experiment)
Hard to Handle (noted for intensity despite sloppy drumming)
poor_songs: It's a Sin (too slow in places)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑'69 set dominated by Jerry’s psychedelic jams and Pig Pen blues; long first half segues into experimental VU‑inspired second set with the backing tape, creating an adventurous but occasionally uneven flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Lead vocals on a blues tune praised; guitar work described as psychedelic finest and tone noted as strong throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Featured prominently on Viola Lee; occasional backup vocal on Silver Threads mentioned, bass generally solid though rhythm section sometimes messy.
band_member_comments.Bob: Provides lead vocal on the blues number; his presence less highlighted but contributes to overall drive.
band_member_comments.Drums: Sloppy drumming noted on Hard to Handle and some sections of the second set; otherwise drives the extended jams.
